horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build explainers and multimedia samples for junior science writing, research communication and public-engagement roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Choose a focus such as health, climate, space, biodiversity, physics, biotechnology or science policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior science communicator, research communications lead, documentary producer or public-engagement manager.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine evidence literacy, audience research, clear storytelling and responsible communication of uncertainty.

blocks.text: Learn to explain scientific discoveries, technology, health, climate and research in ways that are accurate, accessible and interesting to public audiences across articles, podcasts, video, events and digital media.

blocks.label: Course-to-career mapping
blocks.text: Science Communicator is closely aligned with the science journalism focus named in your course. The exact official taxonomy role list could not be independently verified, so this mapping is provisional.

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap uses 2026–2030 as a four-year planning horizon. If your degree is three years, complete the core portfolio and internship milestones by graduation and treat the fourth-year activities as optional extensions.
These are planning outputs;

rows.text: Learn news writing, source evaluation, basic scientific terminology and plain-language explanation.
Write three 400–600-word explainers with linked primary sources.
Practise interviewing researchers and translating technical explanations for general readers.
Record and transcribe a short researcher interview, then produce a clear written summary.
Learn how scientific studies work: research questions, methods, limitations and uncertainty.
Explain one published study and distinguish its findings from its limitations.
Produce an audio or video explainer with accurate narration, visuals and source notes.
Publish a 3–5-minute explainer with transcript, citations and accessible captions where relevant.
Choose a beat such as climate, space, health, technology or biodiversity.
IPCC or WHO for relevant topic areas
Build a beat guide with key institutions, terminology and reliable expert sources.
Report a research story with expert interviews and independent verification.
PubMed for biomedical research; use field-appropriate primary sources elsewhere
Publish a reported feature with a source log and a section explaining uncertainty.
Complete a science newsroom, museum, university or research-communications placement.
Indian Institute of Science for institutional research and communication context
Produce three reviewed pieces and obtain supervisor feedback.
Assemble a portfolio and pitch to science publications, research institutions or public-engagement teams.
Portfolio with five pieces across at least two formats and a short professional profile.

blocks.label: Four-year honours variant
blocks.text: If your institution offers a four-year honours route, use the extra time for a research-backed science documentary, a public-engagement project, audience research or an extended placement with a university or research organisation. Confirm the degree structure with your institution.
Specialisation lanes

rows.text: Study interpretation, risk communication, evidence checks and ethical interviews
Climate evidence, data interpretation, field reporting and policy context
Mission information, scientific terminology, diagrams and expert interviews
Research summaries, press materials, expert liaison and editorial review
Scripting, recording, editing, visual explanation and audience design

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Develop a reputation for making complex evidence understandable without removing important caveats. Learn to assess study quality, explain uncertainty and correct misleading claims. Use AI-assisted research and production only with source verification, appropriate disclosure and respect for copyright and privacy.

blocks.label: Eligibility note
blocks.text: Check whether a placement accepts journalism undergraduates or requires a science degree. Some research internships are restricted to students in science disciplines; a communications placement may have different criteria. For science communication, the most valuable evidence is the ability to explain research accurately, assess evidence and adapt content to an audience. Certificates can supplement that portfolio.

blocks.label: Job-posting note
blocks.text: Review live vacancies and record repeated requirements such as subject knowledge, language skills, writing samples, editing tools and whether a science degree is mandatory. Never claim scientific expertise beyond your training; consult qualified experts when reporting specialist subjects.

A postgraduate degree is optional for science communication. It may help if you want to specialise in science writing, health communication, public engagement, science policy or research communication. Some technical programmes require a science background.

blocks.text: Scholarships and fellowships

blocks.label: National Scholarship Portal schemes
blocks.text: Eligibility depends on the individual scheme, income, institution and academic status. Check scholarships.gov.in.

blocks.label: UGC scholarships and fellowships
blocks.text: Each scheme has its own academic and eligibility requirements. Check UGC.

blocks.label: Fulbright-Nehru Master’s Fellowships
blocks.text: The stated eligibility includes a bachelor’s degree with at least 55% and three years of full-time paid work experience. Verify the current programme and field requirements at USIEF.

blocks.label: DAAD scholarships
blocks.text: Academic results, language proficiency and work experience conditions vary by programme. Check DAAD India.

blocks.label: Institute-specific research funding
blocks.text: Research institutes may advertise funded research positions or communication projects, but eligibility and funding vary. Check the official institute’s current notices.

blocks.label: Sponsorship note

Career progression

items: Years 2–4: Science Writing Intern / Communications Assistant
Years 3–6: Junior Science Writer / Outreach Assistant
Years 10–15: Senior Science Communicator / Documentary Producer
Years 15–20: Research Communications Lead / Public Engagement Manager
Years 20+: Head of Science Communication, independent producer, consultant or educator
blocks.label: Years 1–2

blocks.text: These are indicative experience ranges, not guaranteed promotion dates. Progress depends on portfolio quality, subject expertise, editorial judgement, audience impact and leadership experience.
PhD routes
A PhD is not necessary for most science communication jobs. It may suit a research or academic career.

blocks.label: Science communication
blocks.text: Study how scientific knowledge is explained, received and trusted by public audiences.

blocks.label: Media and communication
blocks.text: Research science journalism, misinformation, digital audiences or public understanding of science.

blocks.label: Health communication
blocks.text: Investigate risk communication, public health messaging or the communication of medical evidence, subject to the programme’s eligibility requirements.

blocks.label: Environmental communication
blocks.text: Research climate communication, environmental narratives or public engagement with sustainability.

blocks.label: Public engagement with research
blocks.text: Study how research institutions involve communities and communicate uncertainty.
Check each university’s entry requirements, research supervisors, funding availability and whether it accepts applicants from a journalism background.

2040–2046: staying relevant. Build a reputation for explaining complex evidence without exaggeration. Keep learning how to assess research quality, communicate uncertainty, correct errors and distinguish expert consensus from preliminary findings. Develop editorial leadership and audience research skills while using AI-assisted tools only with verification, appropriate disclosure and respect for source rights.
